newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico may tax-exempt some pension contributions.
newsitem.headline: Mexico may tax-exempt some pension contributions.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Ministry on Thursday said it is mulling whether to make voluntary contributions to pension funds (Afores) tax-exempt.
"It's a proposal that we're going to analyse very carefully with different sectors," Tomas Ruiz, head of the newly-formed Tax Administration System, told Reuters.
He said the tax exemption was considered an extra way to boost domestic savings.
The Afores began operating on July 1 after six months of affiliating workers, whose pension accounts were previously handled by the government.

Those insured workers who have not yet joined up with a private fund will have their existing savings handled in a central "concentrator" account at the Bank of Mexico. They have four years to voluntarily moved to an Afore and after that, one will be selected for them. ((--Veronica Galan, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9553))
